meta.audience: The reader; the multitude within the account
principles: A record that names its own omissions
A condition attached to receiving more
A community described in four short verses

world_behind.title: The expounding is summarized, not reproduced
world_behind.text: Verse 1 says he expounded all things, great and small, and the words are not given.

world_behind.title: The reason for the Malachi chapters is stated
world_behind.text: Verse 2 says the Father commanded it because they had not those scriptures.

world_behind.title: The subject runs to the end of the world
world_behind.text: Verses 3 and 4 carry the expounding to the elements melting with fervent heat and the last judgment. Mormon 9:2 uses the same picture of the earth rolled together as a scroll, and 2 Peter 3:10 to 12 is the passage both echo.

world_behind.title: Mormon gives a fraction
world_behind.text: Verse 6 says the book holds less than a hundredth of what Jesus taught.

world_behind.title: A larger record exists
world_behind.text: Verse 7 points to the plates of Nephi for the rest.

world_behind.title: He says he was stopped
world_behind.text: Verse 11 says Mormon was about to write it all, from the plates of Nephi, and the Lord forbade it to try the faith of his people. Ether 4:5 and Ether 13:13 record Moroni stopped the same way twice, so both abridgers of this record work under an explicit limit.

world_behind.title: The three days are counted
world_behind.text: Verse 13 says he taught for the space of three days and showed himself often afterward. 3 Nephi 11 through 18 is the first of those days and 3 Nephi 19 through 26 the second; the third is never narrated, which is part of what verse 6 means by a hundredth part.

words.text: Burning, intensely hot. The record uses the word twice, here and at Mormon 9:2, and the King James Bible seven times. Verse 3 uses it of the heat that melts the elements.
Set side by side at an even distance. It appears once, here, in the record, and the King James Bible not at all. Verse 5 uses it of the two resurrections.
One part in a hundred. The record uses the word six times and the King James Bible three. Verse 6 says the book does not hold even that much.
Ordered not to. It turns up twice, here and again at 3 Nephi 28:25, with none in the King James Bible. Verse 11 uses it of the Lord stopping Mormon's pen.
Opened what had been closed. The record uses the word once, here, and the King James Bible once, at Isaiah 35:5. Verse 15 uses it of the ears of the deaf.
Infants and very young children. Its count is twice in this book, while the King James Bible nine times. Verse 16 has them speaking things nobody was allowed to write.
Beyond what words can carry. Treated at Helaman 5:44. The record uses the word three times and the King James Bible three.

phrases.term: He did expound all things unto them, both great and small
phrases.text: The scope of the teaching given in four words. None of it is reproduced.

phrases.term: These scriptures, which ye had not with you
phrases.text: The reason Malachi was recited. The record explains its own inclusion of another prophet's chapters.

phrases.term: Even until the elements should melt with fervent heat
phrases.text: The far end of the expounding. Verse 3 runs from the beginning to the passing of heaven and earth.

phrases.term: Being on a parallel, the one on the one hand and the other on the other hand
phrases.text: Two resurrections described by their symmetry. Verse 5 grounds both in the mercy, justice, and holiness in Christ.

phrases.term: There cannot be written in this book even a hundredth part
phrases.text: Mormon's measure of what is missing. 3 Nephi 5:8 had used the same fraction of a different span of years.

phrases.term: I have written them to the intent that they may be brought again unto this people, from the Gentiles
phrases.text: The destination of the writing. Mormon names the route the book will take back to the people it is about.

phrases.term: Which is expedient that they should have first, to try their faith
phrases.text: The lesser part is a test. Verse 9 makes what is given a condition for what is not.

phrases.term: I was about to write them... but the Lord forbade it
phrases.text: A compiler's plan overruled. Verse 11 gives the Lord's reason in his own words.
The children given speech. Verse 14 says they spoke greater things than he had revealed to the adults.

phrases.term: Which are not lawful to be written
phrases.text: A second class of withheld material. Verse 16 had already forbidden writing what the babes said.

phrases.term: They had all things common among them, every man dealing justly
phrases.text: The economy of the new church in one line. 4 Nephi 1:3 will say the same thing and add what it produced.

verses.label: v. 2
verses.title: A reason given for supplying a text
verses.text: The record explains a delivery rather than simply reporting one: "These scriptures, which ye had not with you, the Father commanded that I should give unto you." What was given is the Malachi material of 3 Nephi 24 and 25, and the stated purpose reaches past the audience present, "for it was wisdom in him that they should be given unto future generations." A document is handed over in one chapter and the reason for the handover is supplied in the next, with the beneficiaries named as people not yet born.

verses.label: v. 6–7
verses.title: A fraction used to measure what is missing
verses.text: The record puts a number on its own incompleteness: "there cannot be written in this book even a hundredth part of the things which Jesus did truly teach." The same fraction is used three other times, at Jacob 3:13, Words of Mormon 1:5, and Helaman 3:14, always for material left out and never for material included. Verse 7 then names where the rest is, "the plates of Nephi do contain the more part," so the omission is presented as a transfer to another volume rather than as a loss.

verses.label: v. 8–10
verses.title: Withholding described as a test with stated terms
verses.text: The record sets out a condition and both of its outcomes. The lesser part is given first "to try their faith"; if they believe, "then shall the greater things be made manifest unto them"; if not, "then shall the greater things be withheld from them, unto their condemnation." Verse 9 also states the sequence as necessary, "which is expedient that they should have first." An incomplete record explaining its own incompleteness as deliberate policy, with a published criterion for release, is a claim that can be held against the record's later conduct.

verses.label: v. 11
verses.title: The editor quotes an instruction he was given
verses.text: The account of what was cut is put in the first person and the instruction is quoted directly: "I was about to write them, all which were engraven upon the plates of Nephi, but the Lord forbade it, saying: I will try the faith of my people." The same construction returns at 3 Nephi 28:25, where the names of the three are withheld and the record again reports "the Lord forbade." Twice in three chapters the writer records an editorial order rather than the material it removed.

verses.label: v. 21
verses.title: A name recorded for a group
verses.text: The last verse of the chapter supplies a label and the criterion for belonging to it: "they who were baptized in the name of Jesus were called the church of Christ." No founding, no organization, and no officers are described; the name follows from an act. The record has used the term before, at Mosiah 18:17, where Alma's converts at the waters of Mormon "were called the church of God, or the church of Christ, from that time forward." That verse offers two names and this one keeps the second, so what happens here is a narrowing of an older usage and not a coinage.

chapter.title: The chapter is mostly about what is absent
chapter.text: Verses 1, 6, 11, 16, and 18 each mark material that was not written down. The record keeps pointing past itself.

chapter.title: A fraction is given rather than a description
chapter.text: Verse 6 says not a hundredth part. Mormon quantifies the omission instead of apologizing for it.

chapter.title: Withholding is presented as a test
chapter.text: Verses 9 and 10 make belief in the lesser part the condition for the greater. The gap has a stated purpose.

chapter.title: The compiler says he was overruled
chapter.text: Verse 11 has Mormon intending to write it all. The record shows its editor being told no.

chapter.title: Children are the ones who speak the greatest things
chapter.text: Verse 14 says they said more than he had revealed to the adults. Verse 16 adds that babes did it too.

chapter.title: Two ascensions are counted
chapter.text: Verse 15 calls this the second time he showed himself. The chapter keeps track of the visits.

chapter.title: The healing list is given as a summary
chapter.text: Verse 15 names the sick, lame, blind, and deaf and adds a man raised from the dead. What took 3 Nephi 17 many verses is compressed here.

chapter.title: The chapter ends with a name
chapter.text: Verse 21 says those baptized were called the church of Christ. That name will be argued over in 3 Nephi 27.

applications.title: Some things are supplied for people not yet born
applications.text: The scriptures they lacked were given because it was wisdom in the Father that future generations should have them. Work with no present use to you can still be the reason it was assigned.

applications.title: Say what you left out
applications.text: Mormon names the fraction. An honest account marks its own limits rather than presenting itself as complete.

applications.title: Take the smaller thing seriously first
applications.text: The lesser part is given to try faith. How you treat what you already have decides what comes next.

applications.title: Accept being told no
applications.text: Mormon planned to write it all and stopped. Someone else's judgment about scope is worth obeying.

applications.title: The extraordinary days were followed by ordinary visits
applications.text: After three days of teaching he showed himself to them often, and broke bread and blessed it often. What holds a community together is usually the repeated small version of whatever started it.

applications.title: Listen to the youngest people in the room
applications.text: The children said greater things than the adults had heard. The chapter records it without explanation.

applications.title: Deal justly one with another
applications.text: They ministered to each other, had all things common, and every man dealt justly with every other. The economic arrangement and the individual conduct are reported in the same breath, and neither is offered without the other.

applications.title: Notice what the group ended up being called
applications.text: Those baptized in the name of Jesus were called the church of Christ, and that is the chapter's closing line. A name earned by what a group actually did is worth more than one it picked for itself.

questions.text: What have I been given that I did not have and did not ask for?
What in my own account have I left out?
What am I doing with the lesser part I already hold?
When was I told to stop, and did I?
What has a child told me that I dismissed?
What would having all things common cost me?
What am I called, and does it match what I do?
